claims.text: Catalytic activity in ethanol oxidation on nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts is governed by composition-induced shifts in the surface d-band center.
Increasing the local Pt concentration relative to Ru alters the catalyst's local electronic structure.
Increasing Pt relative to Ru shifts the surface d-band center.
A shift in the surface d-band center modulates the binding energies of adsorbed CO and acetaldehyde.
The proposed electronic-structure change optimizes the adsorption energies of key ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
The Pt-enriched catalyst will bind poisoning intermediates more weakly than the equal-molar catalyst.
Weaker adsorption of poisoning intermediates will reduce their buildup on the catalyst surface.
Reduced buildup of poisoning intermediates will clear active sites more rapidly.
More rapid clearing of active sites will increase turnover frequency.
Increasing Pt relative to Ru will increase ethanol conversion rate relative to the equal-molar catalyst.
Electronic tuning produced by Pt enrichment will stabilize the catalyst during operation.
Increasing Pt relative to Ru will improve durability relative to the equal-molar catalyst.
The baseline catalyst has equal molar fractions of Pt, Pd, Rh, Ru, Ir, and Os and retains a solid-solution structure.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to solid-solution particles smaller than 10 nm under ethanol oxidation at 130–150°C in an oxygenated atmosphere.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when particle size or reaction conditions change significantly.
XPS can be used in the proposed experiment to quantify the relevant d-band-center positions.
